title: The ML-solver's benchmark: any answerer on verified invented problems, scored against their planted truth
request: Phase 5: a model very good at solving ML problems needs a measurement before any training run.
spec: dclab_rnd/lake/benchmark.py (python -m dclab_rnd.lake benchmark), the gateway purpose solver_answer with its prompt file, evidence/campaigns/solver_v1.
plan: Score against the replica's planted facts, never DCLab's own answer.
One prompt file for training and serving.
Read the sealed split once per answerer and model.

decisions.decision: The truth is the replica's facts, so the rules are measured too.
decisions.why: Scoring against DCLab's answer would make the rules perfect by definition.

change: benchmark.py, __main__, selfplay (the prompt file), prompts/solver_answer.md, models/settings.py, agents/harness.py, tests.

findings.defect: The new contracts' frozen schemas did not match their final shape.
findings.scenario: The baseline was written before the contracts' last fields (the sealed flag, the evaluation kind).
findings.cause: core-schemas never rewrites an existing baseline.
findings.fix: The never-released v1 baselines were regenerated once.

findings.defect: The research index was stale twice.
findings.scenario: A new file in the research folder after the index was built.
findings.cause: The index was regenerated before the runbook was written.

findings.defect: A new model purpose had no data-limit test.
findings.scenario: The suite requires each purpose to prove it sends no cell value.
findings.cause: The purpose was added without its test.
findings.fix: The solver's questions, built as self-play builds them on a table of marked values, reach the model with no value.

outcome: A benchmark any answerer can be judged on, with intervals, before and after training.
lessons: Score a model against a truth the system did not write.
risks: Until the self-play volume run, the dev and sealed splits are small.
